subject: Order form + DPA: export control carveouts, SCCs and onboarding checkpoints
messages:
From: Claire Nash <claire.nash@vitalityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vitality Legal <legal@vitalityhealth.com>, Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@procurex.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Order form + DPA — a few open items

Ben — thanks for the call earlier. We've kicked off legal review and have a short list of must-fix items before procurement will approve: 

1) Export controls / transfer carveouts — we need explicit language for EU-to-US processing and whether any model training data is included.
2) SCCs — confirm which version Redwood will adopt and whether the DPA will reference a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA).
3) Subprocessor role mapping — procurement wants a clearer map showing which Redwood components are "processor" vs "subprocessor" and the subproc list.
4) Order form SOW — we need a timeline for onboarding milestones and an SLA credit clause for missed latency targets.

I attached the internal procurement checklist — can you loop in your legal and let us know timeframe for redlines? We ideally want an updated DPA by Wed so we can route to our GC.

Claire
Claire Nash
Head of Procurement, Vitality Health
[Attachment: vitality_procurement_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 28 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nash <claire.nash@vitalityhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA — a few open items

Claire — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Laura (privacy counsel) and Monica (CS) to confirm. Quick notes from our side: 

- Export controls: Redwood does not train on customer data; processing occurs on dedicated inference instances. We'll propose explicit language to state no model-training of customer-provided inputs.
- SCCs: We intend to adopt the latest EC standard clauses where applicable; we can include a TIA as an exhibit if Vitality requires it.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide a role matrix (processor vs subprocessor) and current subproc list — standard change-notice applies for new entrants.
- SLA onboarding: Monica — can you draft milestone timeline (PO receipt -> infra provisioning -> pilot -> GA) and default SLA credit language we can accept?

Laura, Karthik — can you review the procurement checklist Claire attached and confirm whether the DPA redline can land by Wed (2026-11-11)? If not, propose an escalation path.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Vitality procurement checklist — quick triage

Team — I reviewed Claire's checklist and highlighted three negotiation points that will take collaborator input: 

A) Export controls and training carveout wording — Laura's take: accept explicit "no training on Customer Data" clause; add cross-reference in security exhibit that keys out telemetry/metrics if applicable. This should be low friction.

B) SCCs & TIA — we will adopt the EU SCCs (2024 rev) by default. TIA: if Vitality wants a formal transfer impact addendum, we can supply Redwood's standard TIA and supporting technical mitigations (KMS, region pinning). Legal to prepare a short memo summarizing residual risk.

C) Subprocessors & roles — need product to sign off on which infra components are "processor" vs "subprocessor". Karthik / Product: please confirm the list and whether any vendor (e.g., caching layer) is categorized as a subprocessor. If the list is long, we'll propose a scoped subset for the Order Form and an amendment process for additions.

Karthik — can you coordinate with infra/product and aim to return the matrix by EOD Tue? Monica — please draft the onboarding milestones Ben requested. I'll draft a DPA redline that incorporates A/B above and attach it for Ben to send to Claire. If we can't meet Wed, propose an escalation to legal leadership (I can loop Markus if needed).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Vitality procurement checklist — quick triage

Hi — product/infra confirmed the role matrix. Summary below (full matrix attached):

- Inference Service (API + model runtime): Processor
- Model registry and model artifacts store: Subprocessor (third-party object storage)
- Observability/metrics (third-party vendor): Subprocessor
- KV cache (managed in-house): Processor

I've attached the matrix and the draft DPA redline. Key asks from Vitality that we adjusted: explicit "no-training" language added; TIA annex placeholder included; we kept the subprocessor change-notice at 30 days (procurement asked for 14 — we pushed back).

Please review the attached DPA redline before I send upstream. If Laura signs off, Ben — you can share with Claire and request their legal to comment by EOD Wed.

[Attachment: role_matrix_vitality_20261110.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18 KB)]
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_for_Vitality_20261110.docx (Word document, 42 KB)]

Thanks — Karthik

From: Claire Nash <claire.nash@vitalityhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vitality Legal <legal@vitalityhealth.com>, Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@procurex.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA: export control carveouts, SCCs and onboarding checkpoints

Ben / team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Legal reviewed Redwood's redline and returned a few editorials and one substantive ask: they want the subprocessor change-notice window shortened to 14 days for any subprocessor with access to EU personal data. I pulled their markup and attached it.

If Redwood is firm at 30 days, Vitality can accept the standard process only for non-EU subproc changes; but they will need 14 days for EU-facing subprocs. Can we agree to a split window and document it in the DPA? That would likely be enough to move procurement forward. 

Next steps: 
- Laura / Ben: consider the split-notice compromise (14 days for EU-impacting subproc changes, 30 days otherwise).
- Monica: once we have agreed DPA language, can Redwood propose an onboarding milestone calendar so procurement can sign the Order Form and trigger provisioning?

I'll await your updated DPA. If timing slips, we may need to escalate to GCs — Sam offered to coordinate timelines on the procurement side.

Claire Nash
Head of Procurement, Vitality Health
[Attachment: Vitality_DPA_commentary_20261112.pdf (pdf, 24 KB)]
